history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: CSV row 2356 duplicates existing record seq 1081 (id mankameshwar-temple-agra) — same temple, the famous Mankameshwar Shiva temple at Rawatpara, old Agra. Identity confirmed: one of the four ancient Shiva temples at Agra's corners, regarded as the city's oldest sacred site; legend says Shiva came from Mount Kailash to see the newborn Krishna and, his wish (mankamna) fulfilled, installed a lingam here. Dedup decision needed — this record adds nothing new.

name: Mankameshwar Temple, Agra
town_description: Agra, on the banks of the Yamuna in western Uttar Pradesh, was the capital of the Mughal Empire under Akbar, Jahangir and Shah Jahan, and is home to the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri. Alongside its Mughal monuments it is an old Hindu pilgrimage centre, guarded — in local belief — by four ancient Shiva temples set at the four corners of the city.

travel.airport: Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyay Airport, Agra (Kheria).
travel.railway: Agra Fort railway station (very close); Agra Cantt is the main junction.
travel.road: Daresi Road, Rawatpara in Agra's old city near Jama Masjid; narrow lanes, parking difficult.

visitor_information.opening_hours: See original record (seq 1081): 5:00 AM - 12:00 Noon and 4:00 PM - 9:00 PM daily (verify).
